entry.note: Confirmed paper is 'Interacting Particle Systems and Random Walks on Hecke Algebras' by Alexey Bufetov (arXiv:2003.02730). QOU .md citation in hecke-markov-interpretation.md cites it for 'Bufetov showed that the ASEP generator is a sum of Hecke algebra elements' — paper title and abstract confirm this is the central content. Scope match.

relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT (arXiv:2003.02730v1, matching the registered entry). Not in the working tree on this branch; recovered from intake commit 98ee815675, sha matches. Cited at folio/quantum-observable-universe/mass-theory/hecke-markov-transition.ts:16 and hecke-markov-interpretation.ts:20, plus a References mention in hecke-markov-transition.lean:29. The citation IS load-bearing: prop:hecke-markov-transition asserts that Hecke generators act as stochastic transition operators with p_+ = q^2/(q^2+1), p_- = 1/(q^2+1), and that the Markov trace factorises as independent one-step expectations; rem:hecke-markov-interpretation asserts the resulting stochastic operator K_i 'targets the Mallows measure'. This document supplies exactly that: it recasts ASEP, M-exclusion TASEP, ASEP(q,j) and stochastic vertex models as random walks on Hecke algebras, and Proposition 2.3 (Section 2.3) states that the Mallows measure is a reversible stationary measure of any such walk. One hypothesis needs checking before the folio leans on Prop 2.3 quantitatively: the paper's Section 2.3 introduces the Mallows measure under the convergence assumption on sum_w q^{-l(w)}, while later sections fix q in [0,1) - two conventions appear in the same paper, and the QOU substrate sits at q_0 ~ 1.11 > 1. This is a convention check, not a defect found.

keyResults.statement: The Mallows measure is a reversible stationary measure of any random walk on a Hecke algebra of a Coxeter group.
keyResults.useForFolio: Sources the 'targets the Mallows measure' assertion in the probability picture of rem:hecke-markov-interpretation.

keyResults.statement: The map i is an involutive anti-homomorphism of the Hecke algebra.
keyResults.useForFolio: The reversibility mechanism behind the stationary measure; relevant to the Markov-property/memorylessness clause (iii) of prop:hecke-markov-transition.

proposedActions.rationale: Record the q-convention check: which of the paper's two q-ranges (convergence of sum q^{-l(w)} vs the later q in [0,1)) applies to Prop 2.3, and whether the substrate q_0 > 1 sits inside it, before the Mallows-measure statement is relied on at q_0.
